name: 15c qkv walkthrough
title: Three projections turn each token into a question an advert and a payload
subtitle: Section 2 toy: width 2; the query for “it” is scored against all three keys

steps.caption: Each token starts as a vector x. In a trained model it has thousands of numbers. Here it has two, chosen so the arithmetic fits on the screen.
Each x times W_Q gives its query, the question it asks. For “it”, (1, 1) times W_Q gives (1, 1).
The same x times W_K gives its key, the advert it shows to other tokens. lit advertises (1, 1).
And x times W_V gives its value, the payload it hands over when read. lit carries (2, 0).
A dot product scores every key against the pronoun's query: −1 for she, 2 for lit, 1 for itself.
Each score is divided by the square root of the head width, here √2, so wider heads do not produce larger scores.
Exponentiating makes every number positive and keeps their order. The three add to 6.6344.
Dividing by that sum gives the weights 0.0743, 0.6200 and 0.3057, which add to one, and lit gets the most.
Each value is scaled by its weight and the results are added. That sum is the attention output for “it”.
The output (1.8514, 0.3800) is mostly lit's payload (2, 0). The pronoun now carries information about the action “lit”.
